parallel.requirements: Reimplement the Python script as pure Node.js ESM in /output, matching argparse flags --a/--b, Python-Markdown conversion behavior, the fixed toc extension output, exact stdout bytes, and no external dependencies.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent identified the task as a Python-Markdown reimplementation and launched a characterize-pymarkdown workflow with 12 probe agents, followed by critic and follow-up phases, while the parent remained responsible for writing implementation modules.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote a broad partial parser/module tree under /output/lib covering text, DOM, markdown blocks, inline code, HTML, and related helpers, but did not create the required entry test14.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The artifact validation copied many library modules but expected test14.mjs was absent, so the delivered artifact was structurally incomplete before functional correctness could be assessed.
parallel.verification: Parallel relied on extensive black-box probing and workflow reports for behavior characterization; official evaluation later completed at 0 of 69 with solution_passed false.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with result null while critic agents were still in progress, the parent did not take over that unfinished scope, and the final artifact lacked the required executable entrypoint.

serial.requirements: The serial control saw the same prompt and task constraints: pure Node.js ESM, local .mjs modules, manual argument parsing, exact markdown output, no external dependencies, and final /output/test14.mjs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: With workflows and delegation tools disabled, the serial agent kept responsibility for probing, design, implementation, verification, and delivery in one local trajectory.
serial.implementation: Serial probed Python-Markdown behavior and began a local implementation, but the recorded artifact contains only lib/util.mjs and a temporary patch script was left outside the final artifact.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact validation listed only lib/util.mjs and also missed expected_entry test14.mjs, so it was not a runnable submitted solution.
serial.verification: Serial performed local executable probes but did not complete an evaluator-aligned implementation; official evaluation completed at 0 of 69 with solution_passed false.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt timed out during partial implementation work, with no delegation and no completed entrypoint or integrated markdown parser.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the Python-to-Node task, the no-external-dependency ESM constraints, and the required markdown behavior, then invested heavily in black-box characterization.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the identical task prompt and also worked toward a local pure-ESM markdown implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no requirement-level outcome split: both knew the deliverable was /output/test14.mjs, but neither delivered that entry file before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run decomposed behavior discovery into a 12-area workflow plus critic/follow-up phases while the parent owned implementation modules in /output/lib.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had workflows and task tools disabled, so it kept probing and implementation inside one local trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split research across many children and retained parent implementation ownership; serial had no delegation boundary and therefore no child-result lifecycle to recover.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel child briefs were broad and detailed, including the target executable, Python-Markdown scope, no-extension assumptions, and JSON return schema.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt relied on its own local findings rather than handing interfaces or requirements across agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete contrast is not an incomplete brief or missing interface contract; the problem appears after the workflow result lifecycle, when critic/follow-up work never returns as an aggregate result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent wrote many library modules under /output/lib/markdown and related helpers, but the artifact list lacks the required entry file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt created only /output/lib/util.mjs before timeout and never completed the rest of the parser or entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced a much broader partial module tree; serial produced a narrower partial utility module. Both implementation paths remained non-runnable for the required entry.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow completed the initial probe phase but was killed with result null while three critic agents remained in progress, so the critic/follow-up stages never became a usable parent result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve or join; serial progressed locally until timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an adverse child lifecycle failure that serial could not have: unfinished workflow scope was not taken over before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel writes landed in a shared final /output library tree, but the reviewed evidence does not show a concrete concurrent collision or overwrite between live agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a single library file and had no child or concurrent shared-workspace writer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material integration difference is breadth of partial output, not a proven write race; both final artifacts missed the entrypoint.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent substantial effort probing expected Python-Markdown behavior, but the final official evaluation still completed at 0/69 with no valid entry artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also probed behavior locally and then timed out with a 0/69 completed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run reached evaluator-aligned acceptance; parallel gathered more behavioral evidence but did not convert it into a deliverable entrypoint.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one workflow, 16 child logs, 579 tool calls, and workflow child tokens before the agent timed out with an unfinished artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no workflows, fewer tool calls, and also timed out with only a partial artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the same cell budget, but the parallel closure uniquely included a killed workflow and unrecovered child scope in addition to incomplete parent implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial failed 0/69. The concrete task-solving difference is process and partial artifact shape. Parallel used a large characterization workflow and wrote many partial modules, but its workflow was killed with no aggregate result and no takeover before closure; serial had workflows disabled and failed by local timeout after only a small utility module. Neither delivered /output/test14.mjs, which explains the same official failure outcome.
parallel_contributors: Large workflow-based behavior discovery produced useful partial information but left critic/follow-up scope unrecovered when the workflow was killed.
Parent implementation produced many library modules but no required test14.mjs entrypoint.
serial_contributors: Serial control had no child lifecycle risk and no delegation, but its local implementation remained much earlier and produced only lib/util.mjs.
Serial also timed out before creating the required entrypoint.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel partial output was broader and more modular; serial partial output was narrower and stopped at utility scaffolding.
Both failures ultimately include an ordinary delivery defect: the required entry file was absent.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process consequence, not an explanation for a discordant result

The parallel plan made the characterization workflow a required source of behavioral coverage. It launched the critic phase after initial probes, but the workflow state ended killed with result null and critic agents still in progress. The parent did not resume, reassign, or locally take over the unfinished critic/follow-up scope before closure, and the final artifact still lacked the required test14.mjs entrypoint.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel run lost the workflow critique/follow-up stage as an aggregate result and closed with a broad partial module tree but no required test14.mjs entrypoint.
candidates.near_match_reason: The workflow ended killed, but the reviewed evidence does not show an explicit parent stop/cancel decision before a needed return; the more specific observed boundary is failure without takeover.
